hook.text: Bogotá couldn't afford a subway. So it built a bus system that works like one.

buildup.text: Bus Rapid Transit gives buses their own dedicated lanes, enclosed stations, and prepaid boarding.

discovery.text: Curitiba, Brazil pioneered BRT in 1974. It moves 2 million passengers daily at a fraction of subway cost.

twist.text: BRT gets dismissed as 'just a bus.' But a well-built BRT line rivals light rail in speed and capacity.

climax.text: Over 170 cities now have BRT. It's the fastest-growing transit mode on Earth.

punchline.text: Give a bus its own lane and it becomes a train.

quiz.question: What makes BRT different from a regular bus route?
options: Dedicated lanes, enclosed stations, and prepaid boarding
